subject: DPA scoping: territorial limits, subprocessor roster, and short-window analytics egress
messages:
From: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@wellbeinghealth.com>

Cc: Data Privacy Team <data-privacy@wellbeinghealth.com>

Subject: Quick DPA scoping question + short analytics window request

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — product looked great. Our legal/privacy group has a few follow-ups before procurement can sign the DPA. High level: we need written confirmation of the territorial scope for customer data and a list of subprocessors that will see telemetry or aggregated analytics. Two specific asks: 

- Can Redwood confirm that customer-requested pinning will keep data in the US region for primary inference and long-term storage? We understand temporary cross-region processing for analytics is sometimes required — what is the defined maximum window (hours) and how is it documented in the DPA?
- For the short analytics window we intend to allow (up to 72 hours for model telemetry/analytics), which subprocessors could potentially receive derivative telemetry or telemetry aggregates? If possible, we need a roster and an example retention/erase workflow.

We are close to PO approval but need this scoped into the DPA addendum (or an annex). Can you loop in anyone on your side who handles subprocessor evidence?

If you prefer a quick call, I can do 30 minutes tomorrow.

Thanks,
Rajiv Sharma
Senior Privacy Counsel
WellBeing Health

Subject: Re: Quick DPA scoping question + short analytics window request

Rajiv — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Aditya (infrastructure) and Monica (legal ops) so we can give a single, documented answer for the DPA addendum. High-level responses below; Aditya and Monica can expand with specifics and attach the latest roster.

- Territory pinning: Redwood supports per-tenant region pinning (US/EU/APAC) for primary inference and customer data retention. For customers who exercise pinning, primary inference requests and persistent storage are bound to the pinned region. We do have a documented temporary processing exception for short diagnostics/analytics described in our operational playbook; we will convert the relevant text into DPA language for the addendum.

- Short analytics window: we typically authorize up to 72 hours for transient analytics when triggered by operational needs (scoped to specific telemetry types and with audit logging). We can narrow this to 48 hours by request — let us know if WellBeing requires a tighter SLA.

- Subprocessors: Aditya will attach the current roster and note which roles could receive aggregated telemetry. We will also include an example retention/erase flow and escalation path for data-exposure investigations.

Action items:
1) Aditya: please attach roster + one-paragraph retention/erase workflow.
2) Monica: prepare a short DPA addendum draft (annex) that includes the territory pinning clause, the short-window exception (48h or 72h option), and sign-off language for subprocessors.
3) Rajiv: confirm whether WellBeing prefers a 48h or 72h max window and whether aggregated telemetry can be used for model improvement.

I can join a quick call if helpful — available tomorrow 10:00–11:30 PT.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Stephanie. Rajiv — attaching the current subprocessor roster and a short technical note. See attachments: WBH_subprocessor_roster_20260715.csv and redwood-region-bindings-summary.pdf (both stubs below).

Key technical clarifications:
- Pinning behavior: for pinned tenants we route inference and persistent storage to the geo region you select. Temporary telemetry export is implemented as a controlled job: a scoped telemetry extractor runs against anonymized/hashed buckets, writes aggregates to a short-lived analytics bucket, and only designated analytics services with explicit ACLs can read it.
- Window enforcement: that analytics bucket is TTL'd; by default the job lifecycle + bucket TTL enforces a 72-hour max lifespan. We can change the TTL to 48 hours at provisioning if WellBeing wants that stricter limit.
- Subprocessor exposure: only the analytics service and the monitoring pipeline (logging provider) see aggregated telemetry. Third-party ML ops vendors (listed in the roster) have access only to aggregates and must pass our subprocessor confidentiality terms.

Retention/erase example (short):
1) Triggered telemetry job writes aggregates to analytics-bucket-wbh-<short-id>.
2) Job completes and marks bucket with TTL metadata (48h / 72h).
3) After TTL expiration an automated job purges bucket and creates an audit event recorded in our control plane.
4) For manual erasure requests we run a targeted purge and provide an audit record within 24h.

Attachment stubs:
- WBH_subprocessor_roster_20260715.csv (columns: name, role, country, description, last_security_review)
- redwood-region-bindings-summary.pdf (short summary of routing rules, KMS control points, and fallback behavior)

Let me know if you want the roster redacted to only show roles and not vendor contact emails.

—Aditya
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
